newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up 5.27 pct on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up 5.27 pct on IMF news.

text.p: Thai stocks closed 5.27 percent higher in active trade on Monday as investors reacted positively to news that Thailand was seeking advice from the IMF and studying if a standby IMF credit line was necessary, brokers said.
The composite SET index closed 34.09 points higher at 680.67 on 8.4 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 3.21 points to 52.01.
Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond also said earlier on Monday that the prime minister and the finance minister agreed in principle to tap loans from the IMF.

"No specific figures had been agreed. We (Thailand and IMF) only discussed it in broad principle," he told reporters in the first statement from the authorities signalling that Thailand had decided privately to accept IMF loans.
"The news boosted the market sentiment, especially among local retail investors, who bought stocks across the board," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
Brokers said investors were now evaluating to see which sectors would benefit if the country decided to take the IMF loans or a credit line.

Brokers said investors bought across the board and focused their buying on three key sectors including banks, which led the counters in terms of value and rose 5.82 percent. The other big gainers included the finance sector, which jumped 7.83 percent, and the communication sector, which rallied 7.78 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, rising nine baht to 180.
Debutante Eastern Water Resources Development and Management Plc ranked fifth on the list, closing at 43 baht against an initial public offer price of 30.
Brokers said they expected the market to continue rising on Tuesday due to the IMF news.
